    Summary and Schedule

    How open is our institution’s research output? Which publishers and transformative agreements account for most of our articles? Is our Open Access (OA) share growing? Library and scholarly communication teams answer questions like these for diverse audiences: for management, for funders and in negotiations with publishers. A spreadsheet or a one-off report answers them once. A dashboard that is generated from code answers them every time the data is updated.

    This workshop explores how to build such a dashboard for OA monitoring with Quarto and the R programming language in RStudio. Quarto is an open-source scientific and technical publishing system: you write text, layout instructions and code in one plain-text file, and Quarto turns it into a finished document.

    The lesson is designed for library and information professionals who work with open access and scholarly communication and who have little or no programming experience. It combines programming and professional skills: learners build a dashboard step by step with code and all exercises are based on tasks and topics from OA practice.

    Learning Objectives

    By the end of this lesson, learners will be able to:

    1. Describe what Quarto is, how a Quarto document is structured, and what a Quarto dashboard is used for in OA monitoring.
    2. Apply Markdown syntax to structure text and to define the pages, rows, columns and cards of a dashboard.
    3. Use R to load packages and data, filter publication records for one institution, and calculate OA indicators.
    4. Create value boxes and plots from calculated OA indicators as dashboard content.
    5. Create a searchable table.
    6. Use YAML syntax to style and customise the appearance of the dashboard.
    7. Render the dashboard, update it with new data and share it.
    Prerequisite

    This training does not assume or require any prerequisite programming skills.

    You need a laptop on which you can install software. Please complete the setup instructions below before the workshop.

    The training builds on several software components (Markdown, R/RStudio, YAML, Quarto), but introduces them only at the minimum level needed to successfully build an OA dashboard in Quarto. If you would like a more thorough introduction to these topics, The Carpentries offer dedicated lessons, like:

    • Introduction to Reproducible Publications with Quarto

    Getting ready

    You need to install R and RStudio and download a data file to follow this lesson.

    Installing R and RStudio

    You need R and RStudio installed and also need to be able to install R packages, create directories, and download files. To do this, please make sure you either have administrative rights for your computer or get help for the setup from an IT administrator at your institution.

    Several Carpentries lessons already rely on R and RStudio, please see this section of the workshop template for instructions on installing R/RStudio for various operating systems.

    • R/RStudio installation on Windows
    • R/RStudio installation on MacOS
    • R/RStudio installation on Linux

    R is the programming language we’ll use in this lesson to calculate metrics and create visualizations for the dashboard. RStudio is the integrated development environment (IDE) we’ll use in this lesson to interact with R and Quarto.

    Installing Quarto

    A stable release of Quarto is bundled with RStudio v2022.07.1, and later. Upgrading to new versions of RStudio in the future will also upgrade the bundled Quarto version (Posit user guide).

    You will not need to install Quarto seperately unless you want to upgrade Quarto out of sync with the bundled version in RStudio. Quarto dashboards require Quarto 1.4 or newer. Recent RStudio versions bundle it. To check your version, open the Terminal tab in RStudio and type quarto --version. For this lesson we will use the bundled Quarto version.

    Updating R and RStudio

    This lesson was developed and tested with R version 4.6.2 and RStudio version 2026.11.0+203.

    If you already have R and RStudio installed, please check if your R version is up to date:

    • When you open RStudio your R version will be printed in the console on the bottom left. Alternatively, you can type sessionInfo() into the console. If your R version is 4.6.2 or later, you don’t need to update R for this lesson. If your version of R is older than that, download and install the latest version of R from the R project website for Windows, for MacOS, or for Linux.
    • It is not necessary to remove old versions of R from your system, but if you wish to do so you can check How do I uninstall R?
    • After installing a new version of R, you will have to reinstall all your packages with the new version.
    • To update RStudio to the latest version, open RStudio and click on Help > Check for Updates. If a new version is available follow the instruction on screen. By default, RStudio will also automatically notify you of new versions every once in a while.

    Downloading the data

    Download the data zip file and unzip it. Make a note of the location (i.e. the folder, your desktop) to which you saved the file.

    This file is based on the Journal Checker Tool articles file from the OPENBIB: Selected curated open metadata based on OpenAlex data set published on Zenodo under a CC0 license.

    The data file was enhanced with open access related data from OpenAlex which are also available under a CC0 license.

    The compiled teaching dataset used in this lessons is a CSV formatted dataset containing the following variables:

    column name description
    openalex_id article identifier given within the OpenAlex database
    doi digital object identifier of the article
    issn_l linking ISSN of the journal the article was published in
    ror Research Organisation Registry identifier of the corresponding author’s affiliated institution
    esac_id ESAC Registry identifier for the transformative agreement under which the article was published
    start_date transformative agreement term start date
    end_date transformative agreement term end date
    publication_date article publication date
    oa_status article open access status
    field primary subject field the article was assigned to based on the classification of OpenAlex
    domain primary subject domain the article was assigned to based on the classification of OpenAlex
    institution display name of the corresponding author’s affiliated institution
    publisher display name of the publisher the article was published by
    publication_year article publication year
